working_definition: Mushroom body output neurons (MBONs): extrinsic mushroom body neurons that receive synaptic input from Kenyon cells within specific MB lobe compartments and relay learned valence information to downstream circuits driving approach/avoidance behaviour. This 257-cell cluster is annotated generically as 'MBON' by mapping to a published bulk MBON transcriptome (Crocker et al. 2016), not by identification of an individual named MBON (of the ~20-34 known compartment-specific MBON types); it is a merged/remainder group representing the MBON class as a whole, not resolved to compartment-specific identity.

best_match.fbbt_definition: Adult neuron that receives synaptic input from Kenyon cells in the mushroom body and has presynaptic terminals elsewhere in the central nervous system (Owald et al., 2015; Li et al., 2020). Approximately 10% of adult central brain neurons are downstream targets of MBONs (Li et al., 2020).

justification: This is a merged/remainder-type cluster per the mapping-brief guidance: the report is explicit that this 257-cell cluster is not resolved to any individual MBON type (there are ~20-34 morphologically/physiologically distinct MBON types per Aso et al. 2014, each with its own FBbt term such as 'mushroom body output neuron 11', 'mushroom body output neuron 23', etc., innervating a specific lobe compartment) but instead represents the class as a whole, identified by similarity-mapping to a bulk MBON reference rather than compartment-specific markers. Per dataset guidance to prefer adult-specific FBbt terms where they exist: FBbt:00047955 'adult mushroom body output neuron' (confirmed current/non-obsolete via OLS) is the adult-restricted version of the generic 'mushroom body output neuron' class, and is the correct parent since this atlas is adult whole-brain tissue. Its definition (adult neuron, KC-input, presynaptic output elsewhere in CNS) matches the report's description of MBON biology precisely at this level. Because no compartment-specific markers were used to resolve this cluster, the honest mapping is this broad, adult-specific parent rather than any individual named MBON.

other_candidates.fbbt_definition: Neuron that receives synaptic input from Kenyon cells in the mushroom body and has presynaptic terminals elsewhere in the central nervous system. It can affect behavioral responses to sensory stimuli.
other_candidates.reason_rejected: Stage-unrestricted parent of FBbt:00047955; the adult-specific child term is preferred per dataset guidance and is an equally valid class-level match for this adult atlas.

other_candidates.fbbt_definition: One of the ~20-34 individually identified MBON types (Aso et al., 2014), innervating a specific mushroom body lobe compartment.
other_candidates.reason_rejected: Individual named MBON type; the report explicitly states this cluster is not resolved to compartment-specific identity, so no single named MBON subtype can be justified as the match.

other_candidates.fbbt_term: adult typical mushroom body output neuron
other_candidates.fbbt_definition: Subclass grouping of adult MBONs with 'typical' morphology (per Aso et al. 2014 classification), as opposed to 'atypical' MBONs.
other_candidates.reason_rejected: Report gives no evidence distinguishing typical vs atypical MBON morphology for this cluster; would be an unsupported over-specification.

recommendation: Map to FBbt:00047955 'adult mushroom body output neuron' as a broad match; this is a merged/unresolved-remainder cluster representing the MBON class in general, correctly mapped at the adult class parent level rather than to any individual named MBON.
